A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAL research. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original detection experiments, component ablations, hyperparameter investigations and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds MCLC evaluations and training-process visualizations. The separately attributed LELCM scores do not affect this assessment.

M1.justification: PAL retains the same three training phases, EPG strategy, coarse outer and fine inner updates, decay factor and EEDM loss. Additional explanations and implementation disclosures do not establish a changed PAL procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use SIRST3, NUAA-SIRST, NUDT-SIRST and IRSTD-1K with coarse and centroid point supervision. The new comparisons and process analyses use this existing coverage.

E2.justification: v3 substantially broadens the direct point-supervision comparisons beyond LESPS: Tables S1-S2 add MCLC across eight backbones, and Tables S3-S4 add LELCM for UIUNet and DNANet. Both point-label types are covered; LELCM scores come from its cited paper.

E3.justification: New Appendix D specifies comparator-specific procedures: all MCLC targets receive the Extended type to avoid requiring true target-area information, while LELCM comparisons use published scores. Existing PAL splits, metrics and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figures S2-S3 examine gradual sample admission and label refinement through training-pool counts every 40 epochs and MSDA-Net pseudo-label evolution examples. The existing component ablations and sensitivity investigations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added result tables and training curves introduce no uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial comparative results for MCLC and LELCM and new learning-process observations. For example, Table S1 reports coarse-point MSDA-Net IoU of 54.71% with adapted MCLC versus PAL's 69.38%. PAL's value already appears in v2 Table 1; all twelve pre-existing tables retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(10), covering sample selection, label evolution and EEDM loss, remain unchanged. Appendix C supplies qualitative motivation without new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: progressive learning under single-point supervision, model pre-start, dual updates, controlled label evolution and strong detection performance. Wording changes do not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix C explicitly connects small, low-contrast targets and sparse spatial supervision to pseudo-label noise and semantic drift, extending the curriculum rationale. Appendix D also qualifies the new comparisons through MCLC's area-information requirements and LELCM's unavailable code.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly specifies 20×20-pixel EPG crops, and Section 3.3 identifies h and w as image dimensions. Appendix D documents comparator configuration and score provenance. These additions improve documentation without establishing changes to existing PAL experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds relevant point-supervision literature, including MCLC, MCGC and LELCM, and expands Section 2's distinction between static pseudo-label generation and dynamic label evolution. PAL's central positioning as an automatic curriculum approach remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized wording edits, new appendix Sections C-D, and added acknowledgements and affiliation information. Former appendix Sections C-E become E-G. Section 4.5 also corrects its Table 6 comparison reference from S6 to S7.

P2.justification: v3 adds four comparison tables and two process figures, renumbers retained appendix displays, and adds zoom annotations to Figure 5. The overall visual structure remains similar. Table 3 introduces a labeling error: the coarse-point nIoU header becomes a second IoU header.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons address gaps in v2's coverage of competing point-supervision frameworks, while process visualizations and the EPG crop-size disclosure make PAL's behavior and implementation clearer. The gains are limited by the adapted MCLC setup and literature-sourced LELCM scores, whose settings are not established as fully matched. Table 3's new header error is a small presentation regression; the retained experimental evidence remains intact.
